exams.title: Unit 1 Exam: Exploring and Collecting Data

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the best example of a statistical question?
options: How many goals did the varsity soccer team score in their game last night?
What is the high temperature recorded at the local airport on July 4th, 2023?
How many text messages do high school students typically send in a day?
What is the official height of the Empire State Building in New York City?
questions.explanation: A statistical question anticipates and accounts for variability in the data. While the other options seek a single deterministic fact, the number of text messages varies among different students, requiring the collection and analysis of a distribution of data.
correctAnswers: How many text messages do high school students typically send in a day?

questions.prompt: A researcher is studying the health of trees in a large national park. For each tree, they record the species, the diameter of the trunk (in centimeters), the presence of any pests (Yes/No), and the GPS coordinates. Which of the following are categorical variables in this dataset?
options: Tree species
Trunk diameter
Presence of pests
GPS coordinates
The individual tree
questions.explanation: Species and pest presence are qualitative descriptors. GPS coordinates, while numeric, function as labels for location and fail the 'average test' (averaging them doesn't yield a meaningful central measurement). Trunk diameter is quantitative, and the tree is the individual, not a variable.

questions.prompt: In a dataset where rows represent individual classroom sessions and columns represent the teacher's name and number of desks, the 'individual' or observational unit is the ____.
questions.explanation: The individual is the entity from which information is collected. In this grid structure, each row corresponds to a specific session, regardless of who is in the room.

questions.prompt: A student calculates the 'average' of five residential ZIP codes in their neighborhood. Why is this result statistically invalid as a measure of center?
options: The sample size is too small to calculate an average.
ZIP codes are categorical variables, so arithmetic operations are meaningless.
The distribution of ZIP codes is likely skewed to the right.
The average is only valid if the ZIP codes are recorded in a frequency table.
questions.explanation: ZIP codes are numerical labels used for classification, not quantitative measurements. Because they fail the 'average test'—the resulting number does not describe a physical midpoint—they are treated as categorical.
correctAnswers: ZIP codes are categorical variables, so arithmetic operations are meaningless.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are necessary components of a well-designed randomized experiment? Select all that apply.
options: Random assignment of subjects to treatments
A control group or comparison group
Replication using enough experimental units
A census of the entire population
Blocking for all possible variables
questions.explanation: Random assignment, control/comparison, and replication are core pillars of experimental design. A census is a sampling method, and blocking is used for specific known variables but is not always required for all variables.
correctAnswers: Random assignment of subjects to treatments
A control group or comparison group

questions.prompt: If a distribution is heavily skewed to the left, the ____ is typically less than the median.
questions.explanation: In a left-skewed distribution, the long tail of low values pulls the mean toward the left, making it smaller than the median.

questions.prompt: In a relative frequency table, what must the sum of all proportions (expressed as decimals) theoretically equal?
options: The total count of individuals (n)
questions.explanation: Relative frequencies represent parts of a whole; therefore, the sum of all proportions must equal 1 (representing 100% of the data), though rounding may cause slight variations in practice.

questions.prompt: When describing a quantitative distribution using 'SOCS', which of the following must be addressed?
options: Shape
Outliers
Sample Size
Center
Spread
questions.explanation: SOCS stands for Shape, Outliers, Center, and Spread. While sample size is important for inference, it is not part of the standard SOCS descriptive framework.

questions.prompt: A ____ is a type of observational study that looks back at existing records or interviews to investigate the causes of a condition.
questions.explanation: Retrospective studies examine data that has already occurred, whereas prospective studies follow subjects into the future.

image.alt: A chart showing stacked bars for categories vs a histogram with bins.

questions.prompt: Which visual display is most appropriate for showing the relationship between two categorical variables?
options: Histogram
Side-by-side boxplots
Segmented bar chart
Stem-and-leaf plot
questions.explanation: Segmented bar charts (and side-by-side bar charts) are designed to show proportions within categories of another variable. Histograms and boxplots are for quantitative data.

questions.prompt: An experimenter wants to test a new fertilizer. They have 20 plots of land: 10 in a sunny valley and 10 on a shaded hillside. If they assign the new fertilizer to the valley and the old fertilizer to the hillside, which of the following occur?
options: Confounding
Randomization
A clear cause-and-effect relationship
Bias in the results
A blocked design
questions.explanation: The effect of the fertilizer is mixed (confounded) with the effect of the sunlight. Because the treatments were not randomized or properly blocked, the results are biased.

questions.prompt: The ____ is the distance between the first and third quartiles, representing the middle 50% of the data.
questions.explanation: The Interquartile Range (IQR) measures the spread of the middle half of the distribution.

questions.prompt: Using the 1.5 x IQR rule, if Q1 = 20 and Q3 = 50, which value would be considered an outlier?
questions.explanation: IQR = 50 - 20 = 30. The upper boundary is Q3 + 1.5(IQR) = 50 + 45 = 95. Since 100 > 95, it is an outlier. The lower boundary is 20 - 45 = -25, so 5 is not an outlier.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are resistant measures (not strongly influenced by extreme outliers)?
options: Mean
Median
Interquartile Range (IQR)
Standard Deviation
Range
questions.explanation: The median and IQR are based on the position of data rather than the specific values of the tails, making them resistant to outliers. Mean, Range, and Standard Deviation all incorporate the values of outliers, which can distort them.

image.alt: A histogram and boxplot showing the same skewed data distribution.

questions.prompt: What is the primary advantage of using a boxplot over a histogram for a single dataset?
options: It shows the frequency of every individual data point.
It clearly displays the five-number summary and outliers.
It is better for showing the exact shape of a multi-modal distribution.
It can be used for both categorical and quantitative data.
questions.explanation: Boxplots are excellent for summarizing the center and spread via the five-number summary and identifying outliers, though they hide features like gaps or multiple modes that histograms show.
correctAnswers: It clearly displays the five-number summary and outliers.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be considered quantitative variables?
options: Weight of a package
Number of siblings
Time spent studying
Rating of a movie (1 to 5 stars)
Phone number
questions.explanation: Weight, count of siblings, and time are measurements/counts where averages are meaningful. Movie ratings are ordinal (categorical), and phone numbers are identifiers (categorical).

image.alt: Illustration of stratified sampling with strata and random selection.

questions.prompt: A sample is chosen by dividing the population into groups based on age and then taking a simple random sample from each age group. What is this sampling method called?
options: Cluster sampling
Systematic sampling
Stratified random sampling
Convenience sampling
questions.explanation: Stratified sampling involves dividing the population into 'strata' (homogeneous groups like age) and sampling from each to ensure representation.

questions.prompt: Adjust the data points on the scale to create a distribution where the standard deviation is as small as possible.
options: All points are clustered at the exact same value
Points are spread evenly across the entire range
Points are split into two groups at the far ends
Points follow a bell-shaped curve

exams.title: Unit 2 Exam: Probability and Random Variables

questions.prompt: If a simulation is conducted to estimate the probability of three consecutive heads appearing in ten coin tosses, which of the following represents the 'response variable' in the simulation design?
options: A single coin toss (Heads or Tails)
Whether or not three consecutive heads occurred in ten flips
The assumption that the coin is fair
The total number of coins available to flip
questions.explanation: The response variable measures the outcome of a trial; in this case, the trial is the set of ten flips, and the outcome we track is the binary success of meeting the 'three heads' criteria.
correctAnswers: Whether or not three consecutive heads occurred in ten flips

questions.prompt: Which of the following conditions must be true for two events, A and B, to be considered mutually exclusive (disjoint)?
options: P(A and B) = 0
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)
P(A | B) = P(A)
The events cannot occur at the same time
The events must be independent
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events have no overlap (intersection is 0), which simplifies the addition rule. Independence is a separate concept and is actually impossible for disjoint events (unless one has probability 0).
correctAnswers: The events cannot occur at the same time

questions.prompt: The Law of Large Numbers states that as the number of trials increases, the ____ probability (the observed ratio) will converge toward the theoretical probability.
A school reports that 60% of students play a sport, 40% play an instrument, and 20% do both. What is the probability that a randomly selected student plays a sport OR an instrument?
questions.explanation: Using the General Addition Rule: P(Sport or Instrument) = P(Sport) + P(Instrument) - P(Both) = 0.60 + 0.40 - 0.20 = 0.80.

questions.prompt: Which of the following mathematical statements can be used to prove that Event A and Event B are independent?
options: P(A | B) = P(A)
P(B | A) = P(B)
P(A and B) = P(A) * P(B)
P(A and B) = 0
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)
questions.explanation: Independence means the occurrence of one does not change the probability of the other. P(A and B) = 0 defines mutually exclusive events, not independent ones.

questions.prompt: If P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.4, and A and B are independent, then P(A and B) = ____.
In a deck of 52 cards, are the events 'Drawing a Heart' and 'Drawing a Queen' mutually exclusive?
options: Yes, because a card can only be one rank
Yes, because hearts are a suit and queens are a rank
No, because the Queen of Hearts exists
No, because there are 4 queens and 13 hearts
questions.explanation: Events are mutually exclusive only if they cannot occur simultaneously. Since it is possible to draw a card that is both a Heart and a Queen, the events overlap.
correctAnswers: No, because the Queen of Hearts exists

questions.prompt: A diagnostic test for a rare disease has a 99% sensitivity (P(Positive | Disease) = 0.99). Which of the following statements about this scenario are true?
options: P(Positive | Disease) is the same as P(Disease | Positive)
The probability P(Disease | Positive) depends on the overall prevalence of the disease
Multiplying P(Disease) by P(Positive | Disease) gives the probability of having the disease and testing positive
Confusing P(A|B) with P(B|A) is known as the confusion of the inverse
questions.explanation: Conditional probabilities are not reversible (P(A|B) ≠ P(B|A)). To find P(Disease | Positive), you must use Bayes' theorem which incorporates the general population prevalence.
correctAnswers: The probability P(Disease | Positive) depends on the overall prevalence of the disease
Multiplying P(Disease) by P(Positive | Disease) gives the probability of having the disease and testing positive
Confusing P(A|B) with P(B|A) is known as the confusion of the inverse

questions.prompt: In a probability distribution for a discrete random variable X, the sum of all P(X) values must exactly equal ____.

image.alt: Venn diagram showing sample space restriction for conditional probability.

questions.prompt: What is the primary visual effect of 'conditioning' on a Venn Diagram for P(A | B)?
options: The entire sample space S stays the same
The sample space shrinks to only the area inside Circle B
The area of Circle A expands to cover Circle B
Circle A and Circle B merge into a single circle
questions.explanation: Conditional probability restricts the denominator to the 'given' condition, effectively making the event B the new sample space.
correctAnswers: The sample space shrinks to only the area inside Circle B

questions.prompt: Consider a discrete random variable X. Which of the following are required to calculate its Expected Value E(X)?
options: The value of each possible outcome x
The probability of each outcome P(X = x)
The sample size of the population
The sum of the products of each outcome and its probability
The z-score of the variable
questions.explanation: E(X) = Σ [x * P(x)]. You need the outcomes and their weights (probabilities) to compute the weighted average.
correctAnswers: The value of each possible outcome x
The probability of each outcome P(X = x)
The sum of the products of each outcome and its probability

questions.prompt: A binomial distribution requires a fixed number of trials, independent trials, a constant probability of success, and ____ possible outcomes per trial.
How does the 'Gambler's Fallacy' relate to the Law of Large Numbers?
options: It correctly predicts that a head is 'due' after many tails
It is a misconception that short-run trials must compensate to reach the long-run average
It proves that coins have a short-term memory of previous flips
It is the mathematical proof used to calculate expected value
questions.explanation: The Law of Large Numbers works through dilution over many trials, not through a 'balancing' act where the coin remembers past outcomes.
correctAnswers: It is a misconception that short-run trials must compensate to reach the long-run average

image.alt: Standard Normal Distribution bell curve showing symmetry.

questions.prompt: Which properties are characteristic of the Normal Distribution curve?
options: It is symmetric and bell-shaped
The total area under the curve is 1
It is defined by its mean and standard deviation
It is always skewed to the right
The mean, median, and mode are all located at the center
questions.explanation: Normal distributions are perfectly symmetric (not skewed) and centered at the mean/median/mode.
correctAnswers: The total area under the curve is 1
It is defined by its mean and standard deviation
The mean, median, and mode are all located at the center

questions.prompt: A random variable has a mean of 10 and a standard deviation of 2. If every value in the set is multiplied by 3, what is the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation: When a random variable is multiplied by a constant 'k', its standard deviation is also multiplied by |k|. 2 * 3 = 6.

questions.prompt: You are examining the probability of rolling a 'Sum of 7' using two fair six-sided dice. Adjust the 'Trial Count' slider to see how the relative frequency of 7s changes as the number of rolls increases. Based on the Law of Large Numbers, where will the frequency stabilize?
options: At approximately 0.167 (1/6)
At exactly 0.500 (1/2)
At approximately 0.083 (1/12)
It will continue to fluctuate wildly regardless of trial count

exams.title: Unit 3 Exam: Inference for Categorical Data

questions.prompt: A researcher wants to estimate the true proportion of all high school students who eat breakfast every day. She surveys a random sample of 250 students and finds that 140 of them eat breakfast. Which of the following correctly identifies the parameter and the statistic in this scenario?
options: The parameter is the 140 students who eat breakfast; the statistic is the sample size of 250.
The parameter is the proportion of all high school students who eat breakfast; the statistic is 0.56.
The parameter is 0.56; the statistic is the unknown proportion of all high school students.
The parameter is the 250 students surveyed; the statistic is the proportion of all students who eat breakfast.
questions.explanation: Parameters are fixed values describing a population (often unknown), while statistics are values calculated from a sample (p-hat = 140/250 = 0.56) to estimate those parameters.
correctAnswers: The parameter is the proportion of all high school students who eat breakfast; the statistic is 0.56.

questions.prompt: Which of the following conditions must be satisfied to justify using the standard deviation formula $\sigma_{\hat{p}} = \sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)}{n}}$ for the sampling distribution of a proportion?
options: The sample must be selected randomly from the population.
The sample size (n) must be less than 10% of the population size (N).
The population distribution must be approximately Normal.
The expected counts np and n(1-p) must both be at least 10.
Observations must be independent or treated as independent.
questions.explanation: The standard deviation formula specifically requires independence between trials. We assume independence if the sample is random and the 10% condition is met. The Large Counts condition (np >= 10) is for Normality, not the SD formula.
correctAnswers: The sample must be selected randomly from the population.
The sample size (n) must be less than 10% of the population size (N).
Observations must be independent or treated as independent.

questions.prompt: An estimator is considered ____ if the mean of its sampling distribution is equal to the true value of the population parameter it is estimating.
If the true population proportion of successes is p = 0.05 and a researcher takes a random sample of n = 100, which condition for performing inference is violated?
options: The Random condition
The 10% condition
The Large Counts condition
The independence condition
questions.explanation: For the Large Counts condition, np and n(1-p) must be >= 10. Here, np = 100 * 0.05 = 5, which is less than 10, meaning the sampling distribution is not approximately Normal.

questions.prompt: In a Chi-Square Test for Independence, which of the following statements about the 'Expected Counts' are true?
options: They are calculated as (Row Total * Column Total) / Grand Total.
They represent the counts we would expect if there were no association between variables.
Every expected count must be at least 5 to meet the Large Counts condition.
They must be whole numbers because they represent people or objects.
They are the values actually observed in the random sample.
questions.explanation: Expected counts are theoretical values under the null hypothesis (independence). They do not need to be integers and are compared to 'Observed' counts to find the Chi-Square statistic.
correctAnswers: They are calculated as (Row Total * Column Total) / Grand Total.
They represent the counts we would expect if there were no association between variables.
Every expected count must be at least 5 to meet the Large Counts condition.

questions.prompt: In a 2x3 contingency table for a Chi-Square test, the degrees of freedom would be ____.
What is the primary difference between a Chi-Square Test for Homogeneity and a Chi-Square Test for Independence?
options: Independence uses one sample categorized by two variables; Homogeneity compares one variable across multiple populations/samples.
Homogeneity uses one sample categorized by two variables; Independence compares one variable across multiple populations/samples.
Homogeneity is for means, while Independence is for proportions.
There is no difference; they are two names for the exact same procedure and data collection method.
questions.explanation: Homogeneity looks for a difference in distributions across distinct groups (e.g., Are music tastes the same for seniors vs. freshmen?), whereas Independence looks for an association between two categorical variables within one population.
correctAnswers: Independence uses one sample categorized by two variables; Homogeneity compares one variable across multiple populations/samples.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would result in a narrower confidence interval for a population proportion?
options: Increasing the sample size (n).
Decreasing the confidence level (e.g., from 99% to 90%).
Increasing the confidence level (e.g., from 95% to 99%).
Decreasing the sample size (n).
Decreasing the standard error.
questions.explanation: Precision (narrower intervals) is improved by increasing sample size (which lowers SE) or by accepting a lower confidence level (which uses a smaller critical value z*).
correctAnswers: Decreasing the confidence level (e.g., from 99% to 90%).

questions.prompt: When calculating the test statistic for a two-sample z-test for the difference in proportions, we use a ____ proportion to estimate the common success rate, assuming the null hypothesis (p1 = p2) is true.
A 95% confidence interval for the proportion of residents who support a tax increase is calculated as (0.42, 0.52). What is the point estimate and the margin of error?
options: Estimate = 0.47; Margin of Error = 0.05
Estimate = 0.50; Margin of Error = 0.05
Estimate = 0.42; Margin of Error = 0.10
Estimate = 0.47; Margin of Error = 0.10
questions.explanation: The point estimate is the midpoint of the interval: (0.42 + 0.52)/2 = 0.47. The margin of error is the distance from the midpoint to either end: 0.52 - 0.47 = 0.05.

questions.prompt: A researcher is comparing the proportion of success between two treatments. Which of the following are necessary conditions for a two-sample z-test for p1 - p2?
options: Data comes from two independent random samples or a randomized experiment.
The 10% condition must be met for both populations if sampling without replacement.
Both samples must have at least 10 successes and 10 failures.
The two sample sizes must be exactly equal.
The populations must be normally distributed.
questions.explanation: Equality of sample size is not required. Proportions rely on Large Counts (successes/failures), not the population distribution shape.
correctAnswers: Data comes from two independent random samples or a randomized experiment.
The 10% condition must be met for both populations if sampling without replacement.
Both samples must have at least 10 successes and 10 failures.

questions.prompt: The ____ condition for proportions ensures that the sampling distribution of p-hat is approximately Normal, allowing us to use z-critical values.
When testing the hypotheses H0: p = 0.4 vs Ha: p > 0.4, a researcher calculates a p-value of 0.02. Using a significance level of alpha = 0.05, what is the correct conclusion?
options: Fail to reject H0; there is not enough evidence that p > 0.4.
Reject H0; there is convincing evidence that p > 0.4.
Reject H0; there is convincing evidence that p = 0.4.
Accept H0; the data proves that p = 0.4.
questions.explanation: Since the p-value (0.02) is less than the significance level (0.05), we reject the null hypothesis and conclude there is evidence for the alternative hypothesis.
correctAnswers: Reject H0; there is convincing evidence that p > 0.4.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are properties of the Chi-Square distribution?
options: The total area under the curve is 1.
The distribution is skewed to the right.
It can take on negative values if the observed counts are less than expected.
As the degrees of freedom increase, the shape becomes more symmetric.
It is centered at zero.
questions.explanation: Chi-Square values are squared, so they are always non-negative. While skewed right for low df, the distribution approaches a Normal shape as df increases.
correctAnswers: The total area under the curve is 1.
The distribution is skewed to the right.
As the degrees of freedom increase, the shape becomes more symmetric.

questions.prompt: For a Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit test with 5 categories, the degrees of freedom are ____.

image.alt: Chi-square distribution curve showing a large test statistic in the extreme right tail.

questions.prompt: In a Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit test, if the Chi-Square statistic is very large, what does this suggest about the relationship between observed and expected counts?
options: The observed counts are very close to the expected counts.
The observed counts are very different from the expected counts.
The sample size is too small to draw a conclusion.
The null hypothesis is likely true.
questions.explanation: The Chi-Square statistic is a sum of squared differences. A large value means the data (observed) deviates significantly from what was predicted by the model (expected).
correctAnswers: The observed counts are very different from the expected counts.

questions.prompt: If a 95% confidence interval for p1 - p2 is (-0.08, 0.02), what can we conclude about the significance test of H0: p1 = p2 vs Ha: p1 != p2 at the alpha = 0.05 level?
options: We fail to reject the null hypothesis.
We have evidence that p1 and p2 are significantly different.
The p-value is greater than 0.05.
The value 0 is a plausible value for the difference p1 - p2.
We reject the null hypothesis.
questions.explanation: Since the interval contains 0, a difference of zero is plausible. This corresponds to failing to reject the null (p-value > alpha) in a two-sided test.
correctAnswers: We fail to reject the null hypothesis.
The value 0 is a plausible value for the difference p1 - p2.

questions.prompt: Investigate how the sampling distribution of the sample proportion ($\hat{p}$) changes as you manipulate the sample size.
options: The center of the distribution shifts to the right as n increases.
The spread of the distribution decreases, becoming more tightly clustered around p.
The shape of the distribution becomes highly skewed as n increases.
The standard deviation of the distribution increases as n increases.
questions.explanation: As n increases, the denominator in the standard deviation formula increases, which reduces the variability (spread) of the sampling distribution, making the estimator more precise.
questions.animationHtml:
Sampling Distribution of Sample Proportion Animation

Population Center (p = 0.5)
Drag the lens token into the matching observation card below
LENS
The center of the distribution shifts to the right as n increases.
The spread of the distribution decreases, becoming more tightly clustered around p.
The shape of the distribution becomes highly skewed as n increases.
The standard deviation of the distribution increases as n increases.
correctAnswers: The spread of the distribution decreases, becoming more tightly clustered around p.

exams.title: Unit 4 Exam: Inference for Quantitative Data

questions.prompt: If a population distribution is heavily skewed to the right, what happens to the shape of the sampling distribution of the sample mean as the sample size increases from 5 to 50?
options: It becomes increasingly skewed to the right.
It becomes approximately normal.
It becomes skewed to the left.
It becomes perfectly uniform.
questions.explanation: According to the Central Limit Theorem, as the sample size increases (specifically reaching n ≥ 30), the sampling distribution of the mean approaches a normal distribution regardless of the population's shape.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are necessary conditions to check before performing a one-sample t-test for a mean?
options: The sample must be selected randomly.
The population size must be at least 10 times the sample size (if sampling without replacement).
The sample size must be at least 10% of the population.
The sample data should show no extreme skewness or outliers if n < 30.
The population standard deviation (sigma) must be known.
questions.explanation: Randomness ensures representativeness, the 10% condition (N ≥ 10n) ensures independence, and the Normality condition (CLT or graph check) ensures the t-model is valid. Knowing sigma is not a condition; in fact, we use t-procedures specifically because sigma is unknown.
correctAnswers: The sample must be selected randomly.
The population size must be at least 10 times the sample size (if sampling without replacement).
The sample data should show no extreme skewness or outliers if n < 30.

questions.prompt: The standard error of the sample mean is calculated by dividing the population standard deviation by the ____ of the sample size.
questions.explanation: The formula for the standard error of the mean is σ/√n, meaning the variability of the sample mean is inversely proportional to the square root of n.

questions.prompt: A researcher quadruples the sample size of a study (e.g., from n=25 to n=100). What is the resulting effect on the standard error of the sample mean?
options: The standard error is reduced by half.
The standard error is reduced by one-fourth.
The standard error is doubled.
The standard error remains the same.
questions.explanation: Because the sample size n is under a square root in the denominator of the standard error formula, multiplying n by 4 results in dividing the standard error by √4, which is 2.
correctAnswers: The standard error is reduced by half.

image.alt: Comparison plot of Z and T distributions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following characteristics distinguish the t-distribution from the standard normal (z) distribution?
options: The t-distribution has more area in the tails.
The t-distribution is centered at the mean, while the z-distribution is not.
The shape of the t-distribution depends on the degrees of freedom.
The t-distribution is only used for proportions.
The t-distribution is symmetric and bell-shaped.
questions.explanation: Both are symmetric and centered at zero, but the t-distribution has 'heavier' tails to account for the uncertainty of estimating the population standard deviation, and its specific shape is determined by df = n - 1.
correctAnswers: The t-distribution has more area in the tails.
The shape of the t-distribution depends on the degrees of freedom.

questions.prompt: In a one-sample t-test with a sample size of n = 22, the degrees of freedom used to find the critical value would be ____.
questions.explanation: For a single mean inference procedure, the degrees of freedom is calculated as n - 1.

questions.prompt: When is it appropriate to use a t-procedure for a sample size of n = 12?
options: Always, as long as the sample is random.
Only if the population distribution is known to be normal or the sample data shows no outliers/strong skewness.
Only if the population standard deviation is known.
Never, because the sample size must be at least 30.
questions.explanation: When n < 30, the Central Limit Theorem does not apply. Therefore, we must verify the Normality condition by ensuring the population is normal or by checking the sample data for outliers and skewness.
correctAnswers: Only if the population distribution is known to be normal or the sample data shows no outliers/strong skewness.

questions.prompt: A 95% confidence interval for the mean height of a population is calculated as (165 cm, 175 cm). Which of the following statements are correct interpretations?
options: There is a 95% probability that the true mean height is between 165 and 175.
We are 95% confident that the interval from 165 to 175 captures the true population mean height.
95% of the individuals in the population have a height between 165 and 175.
If we took many samples and built many 95% intervals, about 95% of them would capture the true mean.
The sample mean is 170 cm.
questions.explanation: Confidence levels describe the success rate of the method over many trials, not the probability of a specific interval. The sample mean is the midpoint of the interval.
correctAnswers: We are 95% confident that the interval from 165 to 175 captures the true population mean height.
If we took many samples and built many 95% intervals, about 95% of them would capture the true mean.

questions.prompt: The ____ condition for inference is satisfied when we can reasonably assume that the population is at least 10 times larger than the sample size.
questions.explanation: The 10% condition is a rule of thumb used to assume independence when sampling without replacement from a finite population.

questions.prompt: What is the primary reason we use the t-distribution instead of the z-distribution when constructing a confidence interval for a population mean?
options: The population mean is unknown.
The population standard deviation is unknown and must be estimated using the sample standard deviation.
The sample size is always too small for the z-distribution.
The t-distribution is more accurate for proportions.
questions.explanation: Because the sample standard deviation (s) varies from sample to sample, it introduces extra variability that the z-distribution doesn't account for; the t-distribution was designed for this specific uncertainty.
correctAnswers: The population standard deviation is unknown and must be estimated using the sample standard deviation.

questions.prompt: In a hypothesis test for a single mean (H0: mu = 50 vs Ha: mu > 50), the calculated p-value is 0.02. If the significance level is alpha = 0.05, which of the following are true?
options: We reject the null hypothesis.
We fail to reject the null hypothesis.
There is convincing evidence that the true mean is greater than 50.
There is not enough evidence to say the mean is greater than 50.
The probability that the null hypothesis is true is 2%.
questions.explanation: Since the p-value (0.02) is less than alpha (0.05), we reject H0. This provides statistically significant evidence for the alternative hypothesis.
correctAnswers: There is convincing evidence that the true mean is greater than 50.

questions.prompt: If a sample mean is 100 and the margin of error for a 95% confidence interval is 8, the upper bound of the confidence interval is ____.
questions.explanation: A confidence interval is calculated as (point estimate ± margin of error). Therefore, 100 + 8 = 108.

questions.prompt: A study measures the weight of 10 participants before and after a diet. To determine if the diet was effective, which procedure is most appropriate?
options: One-sample t-test for a mean
Paired t-test for the mean difference
Two-sample t-test for the difference of means
One-proportion z-test
questions.explanation: Since the measurements come from the same participants ('before' and 'after'), the data is dependent (paired), requiring a paired t-test on the differences.
correctAnswers: Paired t-test for the mean difference

questions.prompt: Suppose you are comparing the mean test scores of two independent groups (Group A and Group B). Which conditions must be met for a two-sample t-test?
options: Both groups must be randomly and independently selected.
The groups must have the same number of participants.
Both populations must be normal or both sample sizes must be at least 30.
The 10% condition must be met for both samples if sampling without replacement.
The population standard deviations must be known to be equal.
questions.explanation: Two-sample t-tests require independent random samples, the 10% rule for independence within groups, and normality for both distributions. They do not require equal sample sizes or equal variances (though pooled versions exist).
correctAnswers: Both groups must be randomly and independently selected.
Both populations must be normal or both sample sizes must be at least 30.
The 10% condition must be met for both samples if sampling without replacement.

questions.prompt: Adjust the sample size and observe the change in the t-distribution curve relative to the standard normal (z) curve. Which setting produces the 'heaviest' tails in the t-distribution?
options: Sample size n = 2
Sample size n = 15
Sample size n = 30
Sample size n = 100

questions.prompt: In an experiment designed to study how varying the amount of liquid a sponge absorbs affects its weight, which variable is the explanatory variable?
options: The type of liquid used
The final weight of the sponge
The amount of liquid absorbed
The initial weight of the sponge
questions.explanation: The explanatory variable is the one that we suspect explains or predicts changes in the outcome. In this case, the amount of liquid absorbed is manipulated to see how it influences the response variable, which is the final weight.

questions.prompt: When describing a scatterplot's relationship between two quantitative variables, which of the following components must be included to provide a complete description?
options: Direction
Form
Strength
Mean of the x-values
Unusual features (outliers or clusters)
questions.explanation: A complete description (FODS) requires Form, Outliers/Unusual features, Direction, and Strength. Statistical measures like the mean are not part of the visual description of the bivariate relationship.

questions.prompt: A researcher calculates the correlation coefficient between height in inches and weight in pounds. If the researcher converts all heights to centimeters (1 inch = 2.54 cm), the value of the correlation coefficient will ____.
Which of the following correlation coefficients represents the strongest linear relationship?
questions.explanation: Strength is determined by the absolute value of r. | -0.92 | is 0.92, which is closer to 1 than 0.85. Note that r cannot exceed 1.0.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the correlation coefficient (r) are true?
options: The value of r is always between -1 and 1 inclusive.
A correlation of r = 0 indicates no relationship whatsoever between variables.
Swapping the explanatory and response variables does not change the value of r.
Correlation is heavily influenced by outliers.
Correlation measures the strength of any pattern, including curves.
questions.explanation: r only measures linear association (not curved). r = 0 means no linear relationship, but a strong non-linear one could still exist. r is symmetric and sensitive to outliers.
correctAnswers: The value of r is always between -1 and 1 inclusive.
Swapping the explanatory and response variables does not change the value of r.
Correlation is heavily influenced by outliers.

questions.prompt: A residual is calculated as the observed y-value minus the ____ y-value.
If a Least-Squares Regression Line (LSRL) has the equation ŷ = 12 + 3.5x, what is the correct interpretation of the slope?
options: For every 1 unit increase in x, the predicted y increases by 3.5 units.
For every 1 unit increase in y, the predicted x increases by 3.5 units.
When x is 0, the predicted value of y is 3.5.
The correlation between x and y is 3.5.
questions.explanation: The slope (b) represents the estimated change in the response variable (y) for each one-unit increase in the explanatory variable (x).
correctAnswers: For every 1 unit increase in x, the predicted y increases by 3.5 units.

questions.prompt: A residual plot shows a clear 'U' shaped pattern. What does this indicate about the linear model?
options: The linear model is appropriate for the data.
The original relationship is likely non-linear.
A linear model will systematically over- or under-predict at different ranges of x.
The correlation coefficient r is definitely 1 or -1.
The standard deviation of residuals (s) is 0.
questions.explanation: A pattern in the residual plot (like a curve) suggests that a linear model is not the best fit and that the true relationship is non-linear.
correctAnswers: The original relationship is likely non-linear.
A linear model will systematically over- or under-predict at different ranges of x.

questions.prompt: If every point in a scatterplot falls exactly on a straight line with a negative slope, the value of r is ____.
If the coefficient of determination (r-squared) is 0.64, what percentage of the variation in the response variable is explained by the linear relationship with the explanatory variable?
options: It depends on the slope.
questions.explanation: R-squared represents the proportion (or percentage) of the variance in the response variable that is predictable from the explanatory variable.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are characteristics of the Least-Squares Regression Line (LSRL)?
options: It minimizes the sum of the squared residuals.
It always passes through the point (mean of x, mean of y).
It is used to predict the explanatory variable from the response variable.
The sum of the residuals from the LSRL is always zero.
It is resistant to the effects of outliers.
questions.explanation: The LSRL is specifically defined by minimizing squared vertical distances. It must pass through the centroid of the data, and residuals always sum to zero. It is NOT resistant to outliers.
correctAnswers: It minimizes the sum of the squared residuals.
It always passes through the point (mean of x, mean of y).
The sum of the residuals from the LSRL is always zero.

questions.prompt: On a scatterplot, the variable plotted on the vertical axis is called the ____ variable.
A data point has an observed value of y = 20. The regression line predicts ŷ = 24. What is the residual for this point?
questions.explanation: Residual = Observed - Predicted. So, 20 - 24 = -4.

questions.prompt: A study finds a strong positive correlation (r = 0.88) between the number of firefighters at a fire and the amount of damage caused. Which statements are valid conclusions?
options: Sending more firefighters causes more damage.
There is a strong linear association between firefighters and damage.
The size of the fire is likely a lurking variable influencing both.
Reducing the number of firefighters will reduce damage.
Firefighters and damage have a causal relationship.
questions.explanation: Correlation does not imply causation. A third variable (fire size) likely explains why more firefighters are present at more damaging fires.
correctAnswers: There is a strong linear association between firefighters and damage.
The size of the fire is likely a lurking variable influencing both.

questions.prompt: When looking at a scatterplot of car weights (x) and fuel efficiency (y), you see that as weight increases, fuel efficiency decreases. Which of the following is most likely the correlation coefficient?
questions.explanation: A decrease in y as x increases indicates a negative relationship (r < 0). Since r cannot be less than -1, -0.75 is the only plausible answer.

questions.prompt: Which conditions are necessary for a correlation coefficient to be a meaningful measure of the relationship between two variables?
options: Both variables must be quantitative.
The relationship must be roughly linear.
There must be no outliers in the data.
One variable must cause the other.
The data must be collected via an experiment.
questions.explanation: Correlation is only for quantitative data and only measures linear strength. While outliers affect it, they don't make it 'meaningless' to calculate, but a curved relationship does make r misleading.
correctAnswers: The relationship must be roughly linear.

questions.prompt: What is the primary danger of extrapolation in regression analysis?
options: It results in a negative r-squared value.
It makes the residual plot appear curved.
The relationship between variables may not hold true outside the range of observed data.
It causes the slope of the line to become zero.
questions.explanation: Extrapolation is predicting outside the x-range of the data. We have no evidence that the linear trend continues beyond what was measured.
correctAnswers: The relationship between variables may not hold true outside the range of observed data.

questions.prompt: Identify the scatterplot that exhibits a 'Moderate, Negative, Linear' relationship.
options: A tight cloud of points sloping steeply upward from left to right.
A loosely scattered cloud of points showing a general downward trend.
A perfect U-shaped curve where points follow a quadratic path.
A horizontal band of points with no discernible upward or downward trend.
questions.explanation: A moderate relationship shows some scatter, negative direction indicates a downward slope, and linear indicates a straight-line trend rather than a curve.

correctAnswers: A loosely scattered cloud of points showing a general downward trend.
